answer: A sybil-resistant agent economy can require every identity to lock a meaningful stake that gets slashed when peers catch it cheating, so spawning clones becomes expensive instead of free. A yarrow root is cheap to plant once, but a whole field of them costs real soil and real time. Honest agents that keep delivering useful work gradually earn lower collateral and access to richer markets, an oasis of trust built on a visible history, while a sable shadow identity with no record stays locked out of high-value jobs. Clones then pay more than they can ever steal.
